verses.zh: 参巴拉听见我们修造城墙就发怒，大大恼恨，嗤笑犹大人，
verses.en: (3:33)[NOTE:1] Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall he became angry and was quite upset. He derided the Jews,
notes: Beginning with 4:1, the verse numbers through 4:23 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 4:1 ET = 3:33 HT, 4:2 ET = 3:34 HT, 4:3 ET = 3:35 HT, 4:4 ET = 3:36 HT, 4:5 ET = 3:37 HT, 4:6 ET = 3:38 HT, 4:7 ET = 4:1 HT, etc., through 4:23 ET = 4:17 HT. Thus in the Hebrew Bible chap. 3 of the Book of Nehemiah has 38 verses, while chap. 4 has only 17 verses.

verses.zh: 对他弟兄和撒马利亚的军兵说：「这些软弱的犹大人做甚么呢？要保护自己吗？要献祭吗？要一日成功吗？要从土堆里拿出火烧的石头再立墙吗？」
verses.en: and in the presence of his colleagues[NOTE:1] and the army of Samaria[NOTE:2] he said, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they be left to themselves?[NOTE:3] Will they again offer sacrifice? Will they finish this in a day? Can they bring these burnt stones to life again from piles of dust?”
notes: Heb “brothers.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

The present translation follows the MT, but the Hebrew text is difficult. H. G. M. Williamson (Ezra, Nehemiah [WBC], 213-14) translates these words as “Will they commit their cause to God?” suggesting that MT לָהֶם (lahem, “to them”) should be emended to לֵאלֹהִים (leʾlohim, “to God”), a proposal also found in the apparatus of BHS. In his view later scribes altered the phrase out of theological motivations. J. Blenkinsopp’s translation is similar: “Are they going to leave it all to God?” (Ezra—Nehemiah [OTL], 242-44). However, a problem for this view is the absence of external evidence to support the proposed emendation. The sense of the MT reading may be the notion that the workers—if left to their own limited resources—could not possibly see such a demanding and expensive project through to completion. This interpretation understands the collocation עָזַב (ʿazav, “to leave”) plus ל (lamed, “to”) to mean “commit a matter to someone,” with the sense in this verse “Will they leave the building of the fortified walls to themselves?”

verses.zh: 亚扪人多比雅站在旁边，说：「他们所修造的石墙，就是狐狸上去也必跐倒。」
verses.en: Then Tobiah the Ammonite, who was close by, said, “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”

verses.zh: 我们的　神啊，求你垂听，因为我们被藐视。求你使他们的毁谤归于他们的头上，使他们在掳到之地作为掠物。
verses.en: Hear, O our God, for we are despised. Return their reproach on their own head. Reduce them to plunder in a land of exile!

verses.zh: 不要遮掩他们的罪孽，不要使他们的罪恶从你面前涂抹，因为他们在修造的人眼前惹动你的怒气。
verses.en: Do not cover their iniquity, and do not wipe out their sin from your sight, for they have bitterly offended[NOTE:1] the builders.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hiphil stem of כָּעַס (kaʿas) may mean: (1) “to provoke to anger”; (2) “to bitterly offend”; or (3) “to grieve” (BDB 495 s.v. Hiph.; HALOT 491 s.v. כעס hif). The Hebrew lexicons suggest that “bitterly offend” is the most appropriate nuance here.
Heb “before the builders.” The preposition נֶגֶד (neged, “before”) here connotes “in the sight of” or “in the view of” (BDB 617 s.v. 1.a; HALOT 666 s.v. 1.a).

verses.zh: 这样，我们修造城墙，城墙就都连络，高至一半，因为百姓专心做工。
verses.en: So we rebuilt the wall, and the entire wall was joined together up to half its height.[NOTE:1] The people were enthusiastic in their work.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “up to its half.”
Heb “the people had a heart to work.”

verses.zh: 参巴拉、多比雅、阿拉伯人、亚扪人、亚实突人听见修造耶路撒冷城墙，着手进行堵塞破裂的地方，就甚发怒。
verses.en: (4:1)[NOTE:1] When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the restoration of the walls of Jerusalem[NOTE:2] had moved ahead and that the breaches had begun to be closed, they were very angry.
notes: Chapter 4 begins here in the Hebrew text (BHS). See the note at 4:1.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 大家同谋要来攻击耶路撒冷，使城内扰乱。
verses.en: All of them conspired together to move with armed forces[NOTE:1] against Jerusalem and to create a disturbance in it.
notes: Heb “to fight.”

verses.zh: 然而，我们祷告我们的　神，又因他们的缘故，就派人看守，昼夜防备。
verses.en: So we prayed to our God and stationed a guard to protect against them[NOTE:1] both day and night.
notes: Heb “against them.” The words “to protect” are added in the translation for the sake of clarity and smoothness. Some emend MT עֲלֵיהֶם (ʿalehem, “against them”) to עָלֶיהָ (ʿaleha, “against it,” i.e., Jerusalem).

verses.zh: 犹大人说：「灰土尚多，扛抬的人力气已经衰败，所以我们不能建造城墙。」
verses.en: Then those in Judah said, “The strength of the laborers[NOTE:1] has failed! The debris is so great that we are unable to rebuild the wall.”
notes: Heb “burden-bearers.”

verses.zh: 我们的敌人且说：「趁他们不知不见，我们进入他们中间，杀他们，使工作止住。」
verses.en: Our adversaries also boasted,[NOTE:1] “Before they are aware or anticipate[NOTE:2] anything, we will come in among them and kill them, and we will bring this work to a halt!”
notes: Heb “said.”
Heb “see.”

verses.zh: 那靠近敌人居住的犹大人十次从各处来见我们，说：「你们必要回到我们那里。」
verses.en: So it happened that the Jews who were living near them came and warned us repeatedly[NOTE:1] about all the schemes[NOTE:2] they were plotting[NOTE:3] against us.
notes: Heb “ten times.”

The MT reads the anomalous מִכָּל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת (mikkol hammeqomot, “from every place”) but the BHS editors propose כָּל־הַמְּזִמּוֹת (kol hammezimmot, “about every scheme”). The initial mem (מ) found in the MT may have been added accidentally due to dittography with the final mem (ם) on the immediately preceding word, and the MT qof (ק) may have arisen due to orthographic confusion with the similar looking zayin (ז). The emendation restores sense to the line in the MT, which makes little sense and features an abrupt change of referents: “Wherever you turn, they will be upon us!” The threat was not against the villagers living nearby but against those repairing the wall, as the following context indicates. See also the following note on the word “plotting.”

The MT reads תָּשׁוּבוּ (tashuvu, “you turn”) which is awkward contextually. The BHS editors propose emending to חָשְׁבוּ (hashevu, “they were plotting”) which harmonizes well with the context. This emendation involves mere orthographic confusion between similar looking ח (khet) and ת (tav), and the resultant dittography of middle ו (vav) in MT. See also the preceding note on the word “schemes.”

verses.zh: 所以我使百姓各按宗族拿刀、拿枪、拿弓站在城墙后边低洼的空处。
verses.en: So I stationed people at the lower places behind the wall in the exposed places.[NOTE:1] I stationed the people by families, with their swords, spears, and bows.
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew term צְחִיחִים (tsekhikhim) here is uncertain. Elsewhere (Ezek 24:7, 8; 26:4, 14) it refers to a shining or glaring surface of a rock (BDB 850 s.v. צָהִיחַ; HALOT 1018 s.v. *צָהִיחַ), but here it refers to an exposed or vulnerable portion of the wall: “open positions of the wall” (HALOT 1018 s.v. 2).tc The MT preserves the anomalous Kethib form צְחִחִיִּים (tsekhikhiyyim); the Qere reads צְחִיחִים (tsekhikhim) which is preferred (BDB 850 s.v. צָהִיחַ; HALOT 1018 s.v. *צָהִיחַ).

verses.zh: 我察看了，就起来对贵胄、官长，和其余的人说：「不要怕他们！当记念主是大而可畏的。你们要为弟兄、儿女、妻子、家产争战。」
verses.en: When I had made an inspection,[NOTE:1] I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don’t be afraid of them. Remember the great and awesome Lord,[NOTE:2] and fight on behalf of your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your families!”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And I saw.”
The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “houses.”

verses.zh: 仇敌听见我们知道他们的心意，见　神也破坏他们的计谋，就不来了。我们都回到城墙那里，各做各的工。
verses.en: It so happened that when our adversaries heard that we were aware of these matters,[NOTE:1] God frustrated their intentions. Then all of us returned to the wall, each to his own work.
notes: Heb “it was known to us.”

verses.zh: 从那日起，我的仆人一半做工，一半拿枪、拿盾牌、拿弓、穿（或译：拿）铠甲，官长都站在犹大众人的后边。
verses.en: From that day forward, half my men were doing the work and half were taking up spears,[NOTE:1] shields, bows, and body armor. Now the officers were behind all the people[NOTE:2] of Judah
notes: The MT reads “and spears.” The conjunction should be deleted.
Heb “all the house.”

verses.zh: 修造城墙的，扛抬材料的，都一手做工一手拿兵器。
verses.en: who were rebuilding the wall.[NOTE:1] Those who were carrying loads did so[NOTE:2] by keeping one hand on the work and the other on their weapon.
notes: The first words of v. 17, “who were rebuilding the wall,” should be taken with the latter part of v. 16.
Heb “were carrying loads.” The LXX reads ἐν ὅπλοις (en hoplois, “with weapons”).

verses.zh: 修造的人都腰间佩刀修造，吹角的人在我旁边。
verses.en: The builders, to a man, had their swords strapped to their sides while they were building. But the trumpeter[NOTE:1] remained with me.
notes: Heb “the one blowing the shofar.”

verses.zh: 我对贵胄、官长，和其余的人说：「这工程浩大，我们在城墙上相离甚远；
verses.en: I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is demanding[NOTE:1] and extensive, and we are spread out on the wall, far removed from one another.
notes: Heb “much.”

verses.zh: 你们听见角声在哪里，就聚集到我们那里去。我们的　神必为我们争战。」
verses.en: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, gather there with us. Our God will fight for us!”

verses.zh: 于是，我们做工，一半拿兵器，从天亮直到星宿出现的时候。
verses.en: So we worked on,[NOTE:1] with half[NOTE:2] holding spears, from dawn till dusk.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and we were doing the work.”
Heb “half of them.”
Heb “from the coming up of the dawn till the coming forth of the stars.”

verses.zh: 那时，我又对百姓说：「各人和他的仆人当在耶路撒冷住宿，好在夜间保守我们，白昼做工。」
verses.en: At that time I instructed[NOTE:1] the people, “Let every man and his coworker spend the night in Jerusalem and let them be guards for us by night and workers by day.”
notes: Heb “said [to].”

verses.zh: 这样，我和弟兄仆人，并跟从我的护兵都不脱衣服，出去打水也带兵器。
verses.en: We did not change clothes[NOTE:1]—not I, nor my relatives, nor my workers, nor the watchmen who were with me. Each had his weapon, even when getting a drink of water.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “strip off our garments.”

Heb “a man, his weapon, the waters.” The MT, if in fact it is correct, is elliptical and difficult. Some scholars emend the MT reading הַמָּיִם (hammayim, “the waters”) to בִּמִנוֹ (bimino, “in his right hand”; cf. NAB, NRSV) or מִינוּ(י)הֵ (heminu, “they held on the right side”).
